summary: The E. coli culture, the Zyppy-96 MagBead extraction (from the Zymo manual) and the Pichia electroporation (Lin-Cereghino 2005, via a vendor reproduction) can all be reconstructed. The paper does not give the DNA input volume, the hygromycin plate concentration, the recovery and plating details, or the yeast colony-PCR method. Each has a defensible standard default and the readout is qualitative (colonies and PCR bands), so none is fatal.

gaps.detail: Zyppy-96 MagBead kit procedure (lysis, neutralization, bead volumes, washes, elution volume and times). The paper only says 'Supplementary Method S5'.
gaps.why_needed: The plasmid quality and yield for electroporation depend on these exact steps.
gaps.resolution: Automated procedure from the Zymo manual: 100 µL Deep Blue Lysis Buffer, vortex 10 s, wait 5 min. Add 450 µL Neutralization Buffer, vortex 45 s. Add 50 µL MagClearing Beads, vortex 10 s, magnet 5 min, transfer about 750 µL cleared lysate. Add 30 µL MagBinding Beads, incubate 10 min at room temperature, vortex 5 s every 30 s, magnet 5 min, discard supernatant. Wash once with 200 µL Endo-Wash (2 min on magnet). Wash twice with 400 µL Zyppy Wash Buffer (2 min on magnet). Dry at 65 °C for 30 min. Elute in 40 µL Zyppy Elution Buffer (10 mM Tris pH 8.5, 0.1 mM EDTA), 5 min at 65 °C with vortexing, magnet 1 min, transfer about 30 µL eluate. Wash Buffer concentrate needs 208 mL of 95% ethanol added to 48 mL.

gaps.detail: Pichia competent-cell preparation and electroporation procedure. The paper cites Lin-Cereghino et al. 2005 and 'as previously described' (Grieß-Osowski 2025), which itself gives no electroporation details.
gaps.why_needed: Cell preparation, buffers, electroporator settings and recovery determine whether transformants appear.
gaps.resolution: I could not open the original Lin-Cereghino paper (PMC returned a captcha page). I used the ATUM lab-notebook protocol, which reproduces it and cites it. Competent cells: grow X-33 in YPD, dilute to OD600 0.15–0.2 and grow to OD600 0.8–1.0. Pellet at 500 g for 15 min at room temperature. Resuspend in 9 mL ice-cold BEDS (10 mM bicine-NaOH pH 8.3, 3% ethylene glycol, 5% DMSO, 1 M sorbitol) plus 1 mL 1 M DTT. Incubate 5 min at 30 °C and 100 rpm. Pellet again and resuspend in 1 mL ice-cold BEDS without DTT. Use fresh or freeze 200 µL aliquots at −80 °C. Electroporation: mix DNA with 50 µL cells in a pre-chilled 0.2 cm cuvette and keep on ice for 2 min. Pulse at 1500 V, 200 Ω, 25 µF (Bio-Rad Gene Pulser II) or 50 µF (BTX ECM 630). Immediately add 0.5 mL ice-cold 1 M sorbitol and transfer the cells to 0.5 mL YPD. Recover 1–2 h at 30 °C and 200 rpm. Include a no-DNA negative control.
gaps.source: https://www.atum.bio/assets/pdf/Pichia_Culture_and_Induction_Protocol6.pdf (reproducing Lin-Cereghino et al. 2005, BioTechniques 38:44-48, PMID 15679083); settings consistent with https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-022-15086-w

gaps.detail: Pichia strain and episomal vector selection. The BOTany paper does not name the strain or the selection concentration for electroporation.
gaps.why_needed: Strain and antibiotic identity define the experiment.
gaps.resolution: Grieß-Osowski 2025 states that episomal plasmids were electroporated into X-33 wild type. Episomal vectors carry hygromycin resistance and liquid media were supplemented with 150 µg/mL hygromycin. It describes an episomal Level 1 acceptor vector, L1_2F_ePH, that follows Plant MoClo syntax. Transformants were grown on agar with the appropriate selection and colonies were PCR-verified.

gaps.detail: E. coli culture for MagBead input: volume, antibiotic and time.
gaps.why_needed: Culture density and volume affect lysis and bead binding.
gaps.resolution: Paper s4.5: 1.6 mL low-salt LB plus antibiotic in a 24 deep-well plate with an air-permeable seal, overnight at 37 °C and 250 rpm. Remove 800 µL for glycerol stocks (800 µL culture + 200 µL 75% glycerol). Use the remaining ~800 µL for the kit, which matches the kit's ~750 µL culture format. Level 1 constructs are selected with 50 µg/mL carbenicillin (s4.4). Zymo's manual specifies 24 h growth at 250–300 rpm.

gaps.detail: Amount and volume of MagBead plasmid eluate added per electroporation. The paper gives no volume or DNA mass, and the Lin-Cereghino protocol is written for 5–20 µg of linearized DNA.
gaps.why_needed: The DNA input affects transformation efficiency and the arc risk from salts.
gaps.resolution: Use 1–5 µL (about 100–500 ng) of undiluted eluate, which is the usual amount for circular episomal plasmids. Keep the DNA volume ≤10 µL in 50 µL cells. Optionally measure concentration by NanoDrop first; beads may remain in the eluate and do not interfere.

gaps.detail: Plate medium and hygromycin concentration for selecting Pichia transformants. The paper gives 150 µg/mL only for liquid culture.
gaps.why_needed: The antibiotic level must separate transformants from untransformed cells.
gaps.resolution: Plate 50–200 µL on YPD or YPDS (1 M sorbitol) agar with hygromycin. Use about 150 µg/mL, matching the liquid selection, or titrate up to about 300 µg/mL. Incubate at 30 °C for 2–3 days. Plate a no-DNA control and expect no colonies. The Zeocin plating scheme in the ATUM protocol does not apply to hygromycin.

gaps.detail: Yeast colony PCR genotyping method (lysis, polymerase, primers, cycling). The paper says five colonies per transformation were genotyped but gives no method, and the Pichia primers are not specified in the text.
gaps.why_needed: The genotyping result is the readout in Fig 3D.
gaps.resolution: Pick a colony into 20–50 µL water or 20 mM NaOH and heat at 95–99 °C for 5–10 min. Use 1 µL as template in the 10 µL Red Taq 2X reaction from s4.2: 5 µL master mix, 2 µL water, 1 µL of each 10 µM primer, 1 µL template. Use primers specific to the Level 1 insert, such as promoter- or terminator-to-CDS primers. Include a no-template or untransformed X-33 negative control. Run on an agarose gel with a DNA marker (the 'M' lane in Fig 3D). The cycling program is not given and defaults to standard Taq conditions.

gaps.detail: Which Level 1 episomal construct(s) were extracted and electroporated, and their antibiotic markers.
gaps.why_needed: The construct identity determines the genotyping primers and the expected amplicon.
gaps.resolution: Use a Plant MoClo Level 1 assembly in an episomal Pichia vector with hygromycin resistance, such as L1_2F_ePH carrying pAOX1-driven sfGFP or mScarlet. The experiment's aim does not depend on the specific insert.

retrieved_details: ZYMO Zyppy-96 MagBead (D4102) automated procedure (https://files.zymoresearch.com/protocols/_d4100_d4101_d4102_zyppy-96_magbead_miniprep.pdf): add 208 mL 95% ethanol to 48 mL Wash Buffer concentrate. Warm the Lysis Buffer at 30–37 °C if it has precipitated. Per well: 100 µL Lysis Buffer (vortex 10 s, 5 min), 450 µL Neutralization Buffer (vortex 45 s), 50 µL MagClearing Beads (vortex 10 s), 5 min on magnet, transfer ~750 µL. Then 30 µL MagBinding Beads, 10 min at room temperature with 5 s vortex every 30 s, 5 min on magnet, discard. Then 200 µL Endo-Wash (30 s vortex, 2 min magnet). Then 2 × 400 µL Zyppy Wash (30 s vortex, 2 min magnet). Dry at 65 °C for 30 min. Elute in 40 µL Elution Buffer (10 mM Tris-HCl pH 8.5, 0.1 mM EDTA; water also works), 5 min at 65 °C with 5 s vortex each minute, 1 min on magnet, collect ~30 µL. Store at −20 °C. Paper s4.5: 1.6 mL low-salt LB with antibiotic in a 24 deep-well plate, overnight at 37 °C and 250 rpm. Remove 800 µL for glycerol stock (800 µL culture + 200 µL 75% glycerol) and use the rest for the miniprep. Beads left in the eluate do not interfere with use or NanoDrop quantification. Paper s4.4: carbenicillin 50 µg/mL for Level 1. Pichia electroporation per Lin-Cereghino 2005, as reproduced by ATUM (https://www.atum.bio/assets/pdf/Pichia_Culture_and_Induction_Protocol6.pdf): BEDS = 10 mM bicine-NaOH pH 8.3, 3% (v/v) ethylene glycol, 5% (v/v) DMSO, 1 M sorbitol; 1 M DTT. Culture grown to OD600 0.8–1.0, pelleted at 500 g for 15 min, resuspended in 9 mL BEDS plus 1 mL DTT, 5 min at 30 °C and 100 rpm, pelleted, resuspended in 1 mL BEDS. Use 50 µL cells per 0.2 cm cuvette, DNA in ≤10 µL, 2 min on ice. Pulse at 1500 V, 200 Ω, 25 µF (Bio-Rad) or 50 µF (BTX). Add 0.5 mL ice-cold 1 M sorbitol, then 0.5 mL YPD. Recover 1–2 h at 30 °C and 200 rpm, plate 50–200 µL, incubate 2–3 days at 30 °C. Include a no-DNA control. A Nature Sci Rep paper confirms 1500 V, 25 µF, 200 Ω and a 2 h YPD+1 M sorbitol recovery (https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-022-15086-w). Grieß-Osowski 2025 (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12281619/): X-33 host; episomal vectors electroporated as circular plasmids; liquid media supplemented with 150 µg/mL hygromycin; YP base is 1% yeast extract and 2% peptone; YPD has 2% glucose; at least three PCR-verified colonies screened; the electroporation protocol itself is not detailed there. Paper s4.2 colony PCR format: 10 µL reaction, 5 µL Red Taq 2X master mix, 2 µL water, 1 µL each 10 µM primer, 1 µL template. Paper s4.6 growth after genotyping: 500 µL YP + 1.5% methanol + 0.5% glycerol + 150 µg/mL hygromycin in a 96-well 2 mL plate, 30 °C, 800 rpm, 80% humidity, 72 h.
